subject: CFA not running - output says there are 0 observations

messages.author: 8e10d5b164ef41b7
messages.subject: CFA not running - output says there are 0 observations
parts:
Hi all,
 
I am fairly new to R, so I'm hoping - and assuming - there is some easy fix for my problem.
 
When I try to run a CFA, I get the warning that the model did not estimate.  Perhaps critically, I also get the output (below) that the number of observations is 0.  Any reason why this would be?  I'm including my syntax, as well as the output I get below.  My data is organized as a data frame.  Does it have something to do with sample size, as the sample is not very large here.  I suppose, though, that I would get a different error if it were a sample size issue.
 
Also, of possible note, when I run the command "typeof" on the variables below, it says they are "double."
 
Thanks in advance for any help you can offer - see code and output below:
 
#CFA for CMS APs
CFACMSap <- '
# latent variable definitions
PriorityCMSap =~ Priority_T1_1 + Priority_T1_2 + Priority_T1_3 + Priority_T1_4 + Priority_T1_5 + Priority_T1_6 + Priority_T1_7 + Priority_T1_8 + Priority_T1_9 + Priority_T1_10 + Priority_T1_11
TopPriorityCMSap =~ TopPriority_T1_1 + TopPriority_T1_2 + TopPriority_T1_3
SelfEfficacyCMSap =~ SelfEfficay_T1_1 + SelfEfficay_T1_2 + SelfEfficay_T1_3 + SelfEfficay_T1_4 + SelfEfficay_T1_5 + SelfEfficay_T1_6 + SelfEfficay_T1_7 + SelfEfficay_T1_8 + SelfEfficay_T1_9 + SelfEfficay_T1_10 + SelfEfficay_T1_11 + SelfEfficay_T1_12 + SelfEfficay_T1_13 + SelfEfficay_T1_14 + SelfEfficay_T1_15 + SelfEfficay_T1_16 + SelfEfficay_T1_17 + SelfEfficay_T1_18 + SelfEfficay_T1_19 + SelfEfficay_T1_20 + SelfEfficay_T1_21 + SelfEfficay_T1_22 + SelfEfficay_T1_23 + SelfEfficay_T1_24
'
fit<-cfa(CFACMSap)
summary(fit)
 
> summary(fit)
** WARNING ** lavaan (0.5-17) model has NOT been fitted
** WARNING ** Estimates below are simply the starting values

  Number of observations                             0

  Estimator                                         ML


--
Best,

messages.author: 0325c6a976085eab
messages.subject: Re: CFA not running - output says there are 0 observations
parts:
Do you tell it which dataset to use?

fit<-cfa(CFACMSap, data=myData)

Also, try telling it to do something with the missing data:

fit<-cfa(CFACMSap, data=myData, missing="ML")

See how much missing data you have:

mean(apply(myData, 1, function(x) mean(is.na(x)))

Will give the proportion of people who are missing on all variables.

Jeremy
